name: Kodo Rock
summary: Kodo Rock is a natural stone monument located in the plains of Red Cloud Mesa, between Camp Narache and Brambleblade Ravine. Standing quietly amid the grasses of Mulgore, it serves as an early pilgrimage site for young tauren shamans learning to commune with the spirits of the earth. Because of its modest silhouette against the rolling landscape, travelers must keep a keen eye out to spot it.

sections.title: A Waypoint on the Mesa
sections.body: Situated roughly halfway along the path connecting Camp Narache to the hostile quillboar territory of Brambleblade Ravine, Kodo Rock is marked by a patch of worn earth at its base. While it lacks the sheer grandeur of the towering bluffs surrounding Red Cloud Mesa, its distinct profile resembles the revered kodo beasts that wander the grasslands. For wandering tribesfolk, it acts as a quiet natural beacon in the windswept plains of Mulgore.

sections.title: Spiritual Significance
sections.body: To the Shu'halo, natural formations often carry spiritual weight. Kodo Rock holds special reverence for young tauren shamans beginning their spiritual walk. Novices are directed here on early rites of passage, using the solitary stone monument as a sacred grounds to commune with elemental forces and honor the natural world before venturing into more perilous reaches of the continent.

faq.answer: Kodo Rock is situated on Red Cloud Mesa in Mulgore. You can find it roughly halfway along a straight path between Camp Narache and Brambleblade Ravine, marked on the ground by a small clearing of bare dirt.

faq.q: Why is Kodo Rock hard to find?
faq.answer: The monument blends naturally into the rolling hills and grasses of the mesa. It is only clearly visible from a relatively short distance, requiring travelers to pay close attention to the terrain and watch for the patch of dirt beneath it.

faq.q: Why is Kodo Rock important to tauren shamans?
faq.answer: Tauren shamans visit the rock during their earliest trials out of Camp Narache. It serves as a peaceful, sacred landmark for novices learning to attune their spirits to the land and the elemental forces of Mulgore.

faq.q: What dangers are near Kodo Rock?
faq.answer: While the immediate patch around Kodo Rock is generally peaceful, heading further northeast leads directly toward Brambleblade Ravine, a canyon densely populated by aggressive Bristleback quilboar.

angles.text: For novice tauren shamans beginning their spiritual path at Camp Narache, Kodo Rock is a vital landmark used to attune with the elemental world.
The stone formation serves as a familiar landmark across the plains of Red Cloud Mesa, reflecting the sacred bond between the Shu'halo and the beasts of Mulgore.
